validation.maxSpeedKnSource: The app reference boat long-standing plausibility ceiling, unchanged since commit a0ba92e (2026-07-14, "Salona 45 polar tables from ORC 2026 certificate"), where it entered as the literal 12 in build_polars.mjs validate(). No narrower citation was recorded at the time and none is invented here. It sits about 12% above this boat own table maximum of 10.74 kn.

anchors.label: beam reach
anchors.source: Research-verified magnitude from the ORC International 2026 certificate pass that produced these tables (Salona 45 "Miles Ahead", AUT 035/26; commit a0ba92e, 2026-07-14, whose own comment reads "sanity anchors (research-verified magnitudes)"). No narrower citation was recorded at the time and none is invented here. Retained unchanged: spec N.6 E3's named-source requirement is what stops a NEW hull inheriting these, and E4 compares against these strings to detect exactly that.

provenance.note: Estimate derived from ORC International 2026 certificate Salona 45 "Miles Ahead" (AUT 035/26) — the ~135% genoa table is a modeled overlay on the certificate configuration (+3–5% light-air upwind/reach, 0 at 14–20 kn, −2% upwind at 25 kn); downwind corrected to white sails via 23-boat ORC non-spinnaker ratio study. Flat-water racing VPP — tune with the performance factor. NOT race-calibrated.

validation.maxSpeedKnSource: Highest independently reported speed for this hull is 11 kn reaching at about 25 kn TWS (cruisingworld.com Salona 44 review); the plausibility ceiling sits one knot above it. A ceiling, not a performance claim.

anchors.label: close-hauled, built breeze
anchors.source: bwsailing.com Salona 44 review: "sailed close-hauled at eight knots" at 18-20 kn TWS holding 40 degrees TWA. Band is the reported 8.0 kn +/-15%.

anchors.label: reaching, strong breeze
anchors.source: cruisingworld.com Salona 44 review: "Reaching: 11 knots" at about 25 kn TWS. The source states no TWA, so TWA 110 is chosen as mid-reach rather than fitted; the band is the reported 11.0 kn +/-15%, clamped above by this boat's 12 kn plausibility ceiling.

anchors.label: close-hauled, moderate breeze
anchors.source: sailmagazine.com Salona 44 review: "easy 7-plus" close-hauled once the breeze built from 8 to 10-12 kn ("8-plus in puffs" is a gust, not a steady state, and a polar cell is steady state). Band is the stated sustained 7.0 kn +/-15%.

provenance.note: Tier C, ESTIMATED - this hull's own jib table (see the salona-44-speedy-go fock note) multiplied cell-by-cell by the Salona 45's documented genoa overlay ramp, i.e. its genoa table divided by its jib table (+3-5% light-air upwind/reach, 0 at 14-20 kn, -2% upwind at 25 kn). The difference between this boat's two tables is therefore a function of THAT RAMP, not of this hull, and carries no information about it - which is why the sail comparison is withheld rather than presented as a finding. Same inherited grid and angles, and the same uncertainty, as the jib table. Flat-water racing VPP - tune with the performance factor. NOT race-calibrated, and never measured against this boat.

Tier C, ESTIMATED - no ORC/IRC certificate and no published VPP was obtained for this hull. Scaled from the Salona 45's certificate-anchored jib table (ORC International 2026, AUT 035/26) by one uniform hull scalar k = 1.020, the square root of the sail-area/displacement ratios: 92.81 m2 and 9,500 kg for this hull against 92.35 m2 and 10,000 kg for the Salona 45, both figures from sailboatdata.com so the measurement basis is uniform. The TWA/TWS grid and the beat and gybe angles are INHERITED from the Salona 45 unchanged - an inherited claim, not a derived one: a uniform scalar cannot move pointing angles, capture hull shape or fix a wrong keel. Typically within a few percent, up to about ten percent in individual conditions; the residual is polar shape, which no scalar corrects. Flat-water racing VPP - tune with the performance factor. NOT race-calibrated, and never measured against this boat.

validation.maxSpeedKnSource: No high-wind speed report was found for this hull - the Yachting World test ran in 6-8 kn true. The ceiling is therefore set from the hull's own published waterline: LWL 13.00 m (Yachting World test data panel) gives a displacement hull speed of 8.8 kn, plus a 25% surfing/reaching allowance, rounded to a whole knot. A MAINTAINER JUDGEMENT, not a measurement, and recorded as one.

anchors.label: close-hauled, light air
anchors.source: yachtingworld.com "Elan Impression 444 review: from the archive": "making just over 6 knots close-hauled in only 8 knots true, and just under 6 in 6-7 knots". TWA 45 is the grid point at the boat's own inherited 42.8-degree beat angle for 8 kn. Band is the reported 6.0 kn +/-15% AT TWS 8. The trailing 6-7 kn reading is deliberately NOT a second anchor: the two together have the boat holding speed (just over 6, then just under 6) while true wind falls about a fifth, a flatness no polar of a displacement cruiser shows - the certificate-anchored donor drops 18% over the same span - so the pair cannot probe a light-air cell. Recorded here so the next reader does not re-open it.

The difference between this boat's two tables is therefore a function of THAT RAMP, not of this hull, and carries no information about it - which is why the sail comparison is withheld rather than presented as a finding. Tier C, ESTIMATED - no ORC/IRC certificate and no published VPP was obtained for this hull. Scaled from the Salona 45's certificate-anchored jib table (ORC International 2026, AUT 035/26) by one uniform hull scalar k = 0.892, the square root of the sail-area/displacement ratios: 77.76 m2 and 10,900 kg for this hull against 92.35 m2 and 10,000 kg for the Salona 45, both figures from sailboatdata.com. ONE SOURCE ONLY, and deliberately: Yachting World prints this model's 100% foretriangle area as 85.7 m2 (the main measured larger), and mixing that one figure in gives k = 0.936 - a 5% shift through every cell of the table, from a reputable source, with nothing downstream able to detect it. The TWA/TWS grid and the beat and gybe angles are INHERITED from the Salona 45 unchanged - an inherited claim, not a derived one: a uniform scalar cannot move pointing angles, capture hull shape or fix a wrong keel. Typically within a few percent, up to about ten percent in individual conditions; the residual is polar shape, which no scalar corrects. MEASURED against the only independent light-air report for this hull: at TWA 45 / TWS 8, where Yachting World recorded just over 6 kn close-hauled, this table reads 5.45 kn - about 9% low, at the top of the band above. Because the scalar is uniform, that relative error is the same in every cell; there is no separate, larger light-air error mode. That is the light-air band where the estimator is weakest and where a sail-versus-motor decision can flip, so treat light-air legs for this boat with particular caution. Flat-water racing VPP - tune with the performance factor. NOT race-calibrated, and never measured against this boat.
